caption:
Our last @phxrisingfc home match together? Quite possibly.

10 years as season ticket members, plus a few years attending Arizona United matches before that. 

In 2 weeks, Callum heads to college out of state. This might be the end of an era 🥹

Day 6-9, Barcelona: Of course we had to visit the Camp Nou! Unfortunately, it’s under heavy construction to expand it to 105k seats, but it was still awesome to see.

The Sagrada Família Basílica was amazing! I was here 30 years ago and it looks so different now. Truly remarkable architectural feat.

We finished the trip with a great meal at a tiny restaurant in the Gothic Quarter called Salterio. Probably my favorite meal of this trip.

¡Hasta luego, Barcelona!
Day 4-6: Kaixo Bilbao! Quick trip to see the city and the Guggenheim museum.
Day 4: a visit to the Bernabéu, home of Real Madrid CF. It’s absolutely massive! Unfortunately they’re resetting the pitch, but still kinda cool to see what’s underneath
Awesome time watching Spain defeat Belgium in the World Cup at the historic Puente del Rey, in the shadow of the Royal Palace and Cathedral. ¡Vamos España!

Day 3: we spent much of the day touring the Royal Palace of Madrid, the Royal Armory, the Almudena Cathedral, and the Royal Crypt. 

Afterwards we walked to the Plaza Mayor for lunch and some people watching, then a siesta before Spain’s World Cup match against Belgium!

Day 2, Toledo: our final destination in a very long, 12 hour day trip. The former capital with multiple architectural influences felt like a medieval town, complete with sword making demonstration. The cathedral was massive! After finally arriving in Madrid around 8, we had dinner and watched France win their World Cup match (we both fell asleep)
Day 2, Ávila: awesome medieval town with massive walls, built on top of an existing Roman wall
Day 2, Segovia: so amazing to see a Roman aqueduct that was in use until the 1970s, the cathedral and castle of Segovia were impressive
Madrid Day 1: Only a half day, but had Tuk Tuk adventures and overview of the city, Gran via shopping, and rooftop sunset. Not a bad start to the trip!
Congratulations @callumj.miller, class of 2026!! You’ve grown so much of the past year and I’m so proud of you. Looking forward to seeing what the future has in store! 👏🏻🎓🎉

I started coworking @cohootsphx in 2010 when they first opened, and I’ve been a member and evangelist ever since. I’ve met so many people and have created so many wonderful memories because of the vision, hard work, and dedication of @poondingo and @sundayenespanol.

Last night, their vision for building a community and coworking space in Phoenix reached a major milestone as they passed the torch to the amazing, talented, and dedicated @jaimeemunozz. I cannot be happier for each of them and for the CO+HOOTS community. Congratulations! Here’s to many more years of success and growth! 🎉
